item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00780","case1_error":"Incorrectly evaluates the correct expression (36 × 0.75) − 16 as 15 instead of 11.","case2_error":"Multiplies individual eggs by the price per dozen without converting 120 eggs to 10 dozen.","reason":"Case 1 miscalculates a correct expression; case 2 uses an incorrect unit conversion relation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00781","case1_error":"Incorrectly replaces 36 × 9 with 432 instead of 324 when evaluating the correct volume formula.","case2_error":"Treats Richard as 20 years younger, implying a current age of −6; he must be older, giving a combined future age of 128.","reason":"Case 1 is numerical evaluation error; case 2 reverses the age relationship despite the impossible implied current age.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00782","case1_error":"Uses Sandi's initial $600 instead of her $300 spending, then gives 2100 although its written expression equals 1950.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported 140 after a correct verbal procedure; the remaining apple count is 20.","reason":"Case 1 visibly substitutes the wrong base and contradicts its expression; case 2 supplies an incorrect number without showing calculations.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00783","case1_error":"Gives unsupported 200 after correct formulas for value increase; those formulas yield $600.","case2_error":"Divides average weights by group sizes instead of multiplying to obtain total weights.","reason":"Case 1's formulas are correct but its final number is unsupported; case 2 explicitly uses erroneous relations for group totals.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00784","case1_error":"Evaluates 48 − 17 − 10 as 11 instead of 21, propagating the error into profit.","case2_error":"Evaluates 8 + 12 + 16 + 4 as 30 instead of 40.","reason":"Both incorrectly evaluate correctly written arithmetic expressions; the different operators do not change the error mechanism.","judgment":"same"}]}
